newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH BROADCASTING CO TO SELL MTV STAKE - PAPER.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH BROADCASTING CO TO SELL MTV STAKE - PAPER.

text.p: State-owned Finnish Broadcasting Company Yleisradio Oy (YLE) is ready to sell its 11 percent stake in Finnish commercial television group MTV Oy, daily Kauppalehti reported on Friday.

"We have no particular reason for owning MTV shares. We are watching price developments. The right time for the sale will be looked at next year," Yleisradio executive Jussi Tunturi was quoted as saying.
If MTV shares stay at their current price of around 10,000 markka per each Yleisradio and its pension foundation would stand to gain tens of millions of markka on the share sale, Kauppalehti said.

This year MTV's profits are expected to fall from the record 75 million markka booked last year, Kauppalehti said. But according to brokerage FIM Securities, the company is still likely to net about 1,000 markka per share, the paper said.
MTV's articles of association impose a five percent limit on voting rights that can be used by a single shareholder, Kauppalehti said.
But it quoted Tunturi and managing director Harri Roschier of publishing house Talentum, another MTV owner, as saying the vote restriction could be phased out in two or three years.
Earlier this week, media group Aamulehti Oy said it had upped its stake in MTV to 18.5 percent.
It bought the 10.4 percent stake held by media company Helsinki Media, which will launch its own nationwide commercial TV channel in early 1997.
